definitions.explanation: A person who listens, especially to a story, speech, or conversation. Emphasizes the receiving role in communication.
The person conducting an interview or asking questions in a dialogue, as opposed to the person being interviewed.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{聞|き}き{手|て}の{心|こころ}をつかむのが{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: She is skilled at capturing the hearts of her listeners.

examples.japanese: {話|はなし}は{聞|き}き{手|て}によって{印象|いんしょう}が{変|か}わる。
examples.english: The impression a story makes changes depending on the listener.

examples.japanese: {聞|き}き{手|て}がうまく{質問|しつもん}した。
{聞|き}き{手|て}の{力量|りきりょう}でインタビューの{質|しつ}が{決|き}まる。
examples.english: The quality of an interview depends on the interviewer's skill.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{対談|たいだん}では、{有名|ゆうめい}な{作家|さっか}が{聞|き}き{手|て}を{務|つと}めた。
examples.english: In this conversation, a famous author served as the interviewer.

notes:
Formed from {聞|き}く (to listen) + {手|て} (person/doer), following the common pattern where {手|て} indicates the person performing the action.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {良|よ}い{聞|き}き{手|て} — good listener
- {聞|き}き{手|て}を{務|つと}める — to serve as interviewer
- {聞|き}き{手|て}の{立場|たちば} — the listener's perspective

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {話|はな}し{手|て} — speaker (the opposite role)
- {利|き}き{手|て} — dominant hand (homophone with different kanji)
- {読|よ}み{手|て} — reader (same {手|て} pattern)
